Before you arrive

Check-in and check-out: Check-in is at 3:00 PM. Check-out is by 11:00 AM.
Pets: No pets, please.
Parking: Parking in front of the building is limited to 2 hours. For overnight parking, use the spaces across the street.
Stairs: The apartments are upstairs. Plan on about two flights of stairs, and there is no elevator.
Finding the entrance: Look for the doorway to the left of the bookstore door, with green tile on both sides. It is at 800 5th Ave.
Door codes: The doors use keypads. We message your door code before you arrive, or you can check in at the bookstore downstairs when the shop is open. The shop is closed Mondays.

Downstairs

A bookstore beneath your feet

The Blessed Fig Tree opened in downtown Antigo in May 2023, in the former Buckalows Eatery at 800 Fifth Avenue. It carries about 4,000 new and used books: history, philosophy, fantasy, Wisconsin and outdoors titles, and a manga section the shop counts among the best in northern Wisconsin.

The owner runs the shop and is usually downstairs during business hours. Ask for a recommendation, grab an unusual snack, or pick out something to read upstairs.

Inside the shop

On the shelves

What you will find downstairs

About 4,000 personally selected books instead of millions of algorithm-sorted listings. Walk in looking for one thing and leave with something you did not expect. Guests are welcome whenever the shop is open.

  • Books, new and usedHistory, classics, philosophy, psychology, theology, science and other thoughtful nonfiction.
  • Fantasy and fictionFantasy, popular novels, BookTok favorites and literary finds, plus dragon and wizard-themed gifts.
  • MangaA selection the shop counts among the best in northern Wisconsin.
  • Wisconsin and the outdoorsNorthwoods, nature, survival and gardening books for the trails outside.
  • Snacks, art and giftsUnusual imported snacks and drinks, art, souvenirs and small gifts.
  • Book clubs and eventsBook clubs, contests and occasional special events. Workshops may return depending on mushroom season. The shop's Facebook page lists what is coming up.
Explore Antigo

A working Northwoods town

Langlade County calls itself the County of Trails, and Antigo is an Ice Age Trail Community. You can spend a day on foot without moving the car.

  • DowntownDiners, pizza, antiques and independent shops within a few blocks.
  • The public libraryDirectly across the street from the building.
  • Springbrook TrailWalking and cycling paths, boardwalks and water views inside town.
  • Ice Age TrailMore than 50 miles of the national scenic trail run through Langlade County.
  • Local historyThe Langlade County Historical Society museum and seasonal events.
  • Forests and lakesHiking, fishing, mountain biking and snowshoeing nearby.
